newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo says may not publish final report on copper.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo says may not publish final report on copper.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Tuesday that while it is cooperating with U.S. and British authorities' investigations of its huge copper trading losses, it has not yet decided whether to reveal the final reports.

"A lack of necessary documents made our internal inquiry difficult, and we have no authority to force other firms to hand over their trading records," Takashi Nomura, Sumitomo's senior managing director, told reporters.

"We're closely communicating with the CFTC and the SIB, and are giving them detailed reports (on the inquiry), but I can't say if we're going to announce the final reports," he said, referring to the U.S. Commodities Futures Trading Commission and the British Securities and Investments Board.
"Legal advisers are recommending us not to announce them, since it can be against Sumitomo's interests," he added.
The giant trade house also said the internal inquiry on the copper losses cost it nearly nine billion yen as it hired legal and accounting experts.
Sumitomo said last June that it lost $2.6 billion as a result of a decade of unauthorised copper trading by former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, who was fired in June 1996.
Hamanaka, for nearly 10 years the most influential trader in the world copper market, has pleaded guilty to charges of fraud and forgery in connection with that case.
Nomura said the cost includes commission fees for financial institutions which helped Sumitomo to liquidate huge long positions Hamanaka has built in the world copper market.
